title: Towards High-Performance Virtual Platforms: A Parallelization Strategy for SystemC TLM-2.0 CPU Models
problem: SystemC TLM-2.0 simulators for full SoCs are single-threaded by default, severely limiting simulation performance despite being designed to model parallel systems. This creates a bottleneck for hardware design space exploration and verification.
motivation: Faster system-level simulation is essential for efficient design space exploration and verification of complex multi-core and many-core SoCs.
method: The approach splits the CPU simulation across multiple processor cores instead of running it single-threaded, while keeping full compatibility with the SystemC TLM-2.0 standard. To avoid slowing down the coordination between parallel cores when accessing shared memory, they cache memory pointers asynchronously (Direct Memory Interface pointer caching) — each core remembers which memory locations it needs without constantly waiting for synchronization. They also add a tunable parameter called async_rate that controls how often the CPU reports timing information to the simulator: more frequent reporting gives accurate timing but slower simulation; less frequent reporting speeds up simulation but sacrifices timing precision.
key_novelty: The key idea is parallelizing CPU simulations across multiple cores while maintaining SystemC TLM-2.0 standard compliance by using asynchronous memory pointer caching to reduce coordination overhead and making timing synchronization frequency adjustable.
contributions: Parallelization strategy for CPU models in SystemC TLM-2.0 virtual platforms
Asynchronous DMI pointer caching algorithm for reduced synchronization overhead
Async_rate tunable parameter for flexible timing annotation frequency control
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the provided abstract.
